runs.name: EquipmentShare.com Inc
runs.entry: Price **$15.085** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged; IPO price $24.50, 424B4 0001628280-26-003334) x **253,375,963 shares** (Class A 215,807,019 plus Class B 37,568,944, same economics, Class B twenty votes and convertible one for one; 10-Q cover for 2026-06-30, 0001693736-26-000020; checked against the balance sheet) = cap **$3,822M**; not in the count: options on 7.0M Class A and 3.4M Class B in the money, 36.65M Class B on the founders' IPO performance units earned at price hurdles of $29.85 to $358.16; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y, 2026-10-09). Primary document the FY2025 10-K (0001628280-26-019656), with the 10-Q to 2026-06-30, the 424B4 (2022 to 2024 statements), the DEF 14A of 2026-04-21 and the 8-Ks of 2026-01-26 to 2026-08-12; total assets at 2025-12-31 $5,987M cross-checked to the filed balance sheet, and the 2024 cash-flow column of the 10-K against the 424B4's. Listed January 2026; construction equipment rental on its T3 telematics platform, more than half the fleet ($5.5B of OEC at 2026-06-30) owned by OWN Program investors who buy equipment from the company and lease it back on revenue share. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs (eight lines: the OWN Program, fleet economics, the expansion, debt and the preferred, competition, related parties, stock pay and control, the construction cycle). `tools/run.py` printed no arithmetic (XBRL only from the 10-K for 2025); every figure taken by hand from the filed statements. **Q1 IN** (equipment rental understood; company-specific doubts sent to Q2 and Q4). **Q2 OUT**: a high-cost entrant in a commodity field: rent per dollar of fleet 28% against United Rentals' 61% (2025, bases not identical, said so); operating income on total assets 4.5% to 5.6% against United Rentals' 13% to 15% (2023 to 2025), Sunbelt 10% to 11%, Herc 2% to 9.5%; the 10-K says customers compare rates online and results suffer if it does not match rivals' prices (price and mix -$46M of 2025 rental revenue); rivals are building their own technology platforms; and its own history, a national network built from nothing in ten years on borrowed money and investors' equipment, answers the attacker test against it. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: extensive dealings with the co-founders' entities (equipment sales $196M, $346M, $128M 2023 to 2025, OWN payouts to them, leases of properties, vehicles and aircraft, a money-market account at a bank they part own); a securities class action filed 2026-07-23 on the IPO's related-party disclosures; the headline Adjusted Core EBITDA adds back $837M of OWN payouts and Adjusted Net Income excludes the founders' own award expense; $179M of 2025's $297M operating income in the fourth quarter, the quarter of a single $447M sale to one OWN investor before the listing, $1M in the first quarter of 2026; the auditor's one critical audit matter is the sale-leaseback accounting; a $500M buyback with no price authorized eight days after $1,350M of 7.125% second-lien notes; in the founders' favour, about $3.8M of open-market purchases by both, June to September 2026. Beneath the stop, COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash after all spending negative in every public year (four fiscal years only, 2022 to 2025; mean -$274.8M all-equity, -$435.6M equity-only); after a depreciation-sized maintenance charge $102.5M, $138.3M, $126.8M, $109.9M all-equity while revenue rose $1.73B to $4.38B; claims ahead of the common $3,871M (net debt $3,501M plus the $370M perpetual preferred, deducted as a CONVENTION of this run); range **-$34.65 to -$6.86** a share all-equity (top -$5.40 without the preferred; equity-only -$31.60 to -$3.82), fair -$18.35 all-equity (-$9.92 equity-only); no positive fair price, not armed. Balance sheets 2023 to 2026-06-30 only (no earlier ones public): retained earnings 25, 8, 0, -47 ($M); debt up $1,379M while owned fleet rose $818M; prepaid costs $18M to $232M with no note explaining them; accrued equipment purchases up $180M in 2025, not said whether inside operating cash; pre-tax income $54M against interest $285M in 2025. Competitors from their own filings (United Rentals, Sunbelt Rentals, Herc, the three the prospectus names; all file, no non-filer flagged). Contamination declared by the analyst: a filename filter over `Test Runs/` for the ticker and name before the template was copied (no match, nothing opened; the self-audit's blind-rule box left unticked); commit subjects, untracked folder names and the memory index in the session context; nothing used. Commits 50d3b760 to b128aed3. Citations: the analyst's check 54 ids, 42 fragments, 0 problems; the dispatcher's script (`fold_cite_check.py`) 54 ids present, 39 fragments, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold. check_framework PASS. Analyst's gaps for the operator: (1) Q2's parts rule meets a sale-leaseback: the sales segment carries more than all of three-year profit after fleet costs but its profit is the markup on fleet sold to the lessors of the rental segment; the analyst read the two as one castle, and the framework could say a segment whose chief customers are the lessors of another is read with it; (2) segment operating profit is defined by the filer, here only adjusted EBITDA excluding the fleet's rent and depreciation, so the analyst allocated those costs (a CONVENTION of the run); a sentence on allocating unallocated costs would make two runs agree; (3) owner cash counts the front-loaded profit on sale-leasebacks to the company's own lessors, which recurs only while the investor fleet grows; the construction has no line for it and it was left in (flattering the figures); smaller: Part VII is silent on a cash-paying perpetual preferred ahead of the common. Not obtained: a fifth fiscal year or any balance sheet before 2023; what the prepaid costs and accrued equipment purchases are; rent per dollar of fleet on identical bases.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: a high-cost entrant in a commodity field, about half United Rentals' rent per dollar of fleet and a third of its operating return on assets (2023 to 2025), price set by rivals, a technology edge being copied, and its own ten-year build-out answering the attacker test against it. Integrity facts recorded: co-founder related-party dealings, a class action of 2026-07-23 on their disclosure, adjusted figures that add back $837M of OWN payouts, and most of 2025's operating income booked in the quarter of one $447M sale-leaseback before the listing. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: owner cash negative every public year, fair -$18.35 all-equity against $15.085 (not armed). The analyst asks how Q2's parts rule reads a sale-leaseback segment.
